claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a BCC solid solution.
High-energy ball milling may introduce oxygen contamination into the powder.
SPS at 950–1000 °C provides sufficient thermal energy to activate diffusion.
Enhanced diffusion at 950–1000 °C drives precipitation of Ti-rich and Al-rich intermetallic phases.
The precipitates may include Mg2Ti, Al3Ti, or Laves phases.
The proposed secondary phases are fine and coherent.
The secondary phases precipitate at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
The precipitated intermetallic phases act as diffusion barriers.
The diffusion barriers restrict magnesium loss during processing.
The secondary phases promote densification and pore elimination.
Precipitation of the secondary phases increases hardness through precipitation strengthening.
The secondary phases facilitate formation of a continuous oxide layer enriched in TiO2 and Al2O3 during oxidation.
The continuous TiO2/Al2O3-enriched oxide layer improves oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Sintering above 1000 °C causes excessive magnesium volatilization and composition deviation.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient driving force for secondary-phase precipitation and densification.
Processing below 800 °C produces porous, weak microstructures with poor oxidation resistance.
Under a diffusion-controlled mechanism, samples sintered at 950–1000 °C will show a continuous protective oxide and parabolic oxidation kinetics.
A sample sintered at 1050 °C will show a discontinuous, non-protective oxide and linear oxidation kinetics because of magnesium loss.
Under a surface-reaction-limited mechanism, oxide structure and oxidation kinetics will not correlate strongly with sintering temperature or secondary-phase precipitation.
